# Status (2026-11-02, updated)

**Question:** which insects traded **alive** online could be invasive plant pests in Norway (later the EU)?

**Scope rules**

- **Plant pests only:** insects, mites, land snails and slugs, apple snails (*Pomacea*) and nematodes. Crustaceans (e.g. *Eriocheir sinensis*), spiders, scorpions, ticks and marine or aquarium molluscs are out, even when EU-listed. Names with unknown class are kept and labelled.
- **Live specimens only:** dead material (pinned, papered, mounted, framed, ex-pupa specimens, collection, bodies, jewellery) is **labelled as dead, not deleted**. Unknown is kept.
- **Per species:** `live` if any live evidence; else `unknown` if any evidence of unclear form (food use, LEMIS unspecified); else `dead` if there is dead evidence; else `unknown`.

| Step | Status |
|---|---|
| 1. Seed species list (Hughes 2026) | Done: 10,682 names (+389 live LEMIS species = 11,071; 10,851 after merging synonyms) |
| 2. Collect live listings (NO/EU) | Shop scripts now label each row live/dead/check/unknown and write to `5_outputs/tables/`. Norway sources not added yet |
| 3. Extract names from listings | Not started |
| 4. Resolve names (GBIF) | Done: 10,752 of 11,071 names resolved; 308 accepted species still have no class |
| 5. Pest lookup (EPPO) | Done: 805 EPPO codes (Hughes + LEMIS) via local SQLite + GDAPI |
| 5b. Scope + life state | Done: LEMIS (all forms), Lassaline use, Wang → `plant_pest_candidates.csv` (3,408) |
| 6. Tier A–D | Not started |
| 7. Pathway / FinnPRIO | Not started |

# Data sources

All raw data sits in `1_raw_data/<author+year_source>/`, and the PDFs in `3_metadata/pdf/`. Full list: `3_metadata/data_sources.md`.

| Source | Local folder | What it gives | Live vs dead |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hughes et al. 2026 | `hughes2026_figshare_33194898/` | 10,682 traded invertebrate names, flags per data source | No distinction |
| Lassaline et al. 2025 | `lassaline2025_sciencedirect/` | 4,738 taxa (4,300 insects) from 91 papers, with `reported_use` | Partly, through use type |
| Wang et al. 2023 | `wang2023_zenodo_7825674/` | 51,348 eBay butterfly sales from 2022, seller country | Dead specimens (inferred) |
| Marshall et al. 2022 | `marshall2022_zenodo_5758541/` | Arachnid web-trade data + R scraping code | Mostly live pets (inferred) |
| LEMIS 2000–2014 (Eskew et al. 2020) | `eskew2020_lemis_github/` | 5.5 M US import records | **Yes**: LIV / EGL / DEA codes |
| EPPO codes + GDAPI | `eppo db/`, `2_processed_data/eppo_api_cache/` | Codes, synonyms, taxonomy, lists, hosts, distribution | n/a |

## Hughes et al. 2026 - wildlife trade data gaps
- *Sci. Adv.* 12:eaei3504, doi 10.1126/sciadv.aei3504. PDF: `Hughes_2026_wildlife_trade_data_gaps.pdf`.
- Supplementary data on figshare: https://doi.org/10.26188/33194898 (https://figshare.com/s/b05b15f87a58dd65eb1e)
- Title of dataset: "Appearance of species in trade data sources: Supplementary data for The true scale of global wildlife trade is obscured by data gaps"
- Also has a preprint on EcoEvoRxiv with supplementary files on Google Drive: https://ecoevorxiv.org/repository/view/11272/ (not downloaded; probably the same data).
- **Local:** `upSetData_singleNames_inv_comp.csv` (10,682 names) with 0/1 flags: CITES Trade, CITES App, LEMIS, LEMIS_noS, IUCN, TRAFFIC, Research. `Data_S1 - sourceSpeciesLists/` holds the raw lists per source.
- **Research flag** = the published studies they compiled: Lassaline 2025 (`inv_trim_1.csv`), Wang 2023 (`but_trim_1.csv`), Marshall 2022 (`ara_trim_1.csv`).
- **Limitation:** none of the flags say whether the animals were live or dead. `LEMIS = 1` covers any form, and 3,836 of the names flagged LEMIS have no live import record.

## Lassaline et al. 2025 - global invertebrate trade
- *Biol. Conserv.* 308:111266, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biocon.2025.111266 (CC-BY). PDF: `Lassaline_2025_global_invertebrate_trade.pdf`.
- Data availability (from PDF): "The data supporting the findings of this study are available within the article and its supplementary materials."
- No external repository (Zenodo/figshare). The data is only in the supplementary appendix on ScienceDirect, downloaded by hand on 2026-11-02.
- Note: the figshare link 10.6084/m9.figshare.22115045 that appears in searches is for a DIFFERENT Lassaline paper (2023, Austral Entomology, "Untangling the web").
- **Local:** `mmc4.xlsx` holds 4,738 GBIF-resolved taxa with `reported_use` and source article. `mmc1`–`mmc3.docx` hold search terms and included/excluded literature.
- **Use as a stand-in for live/dead:** collection (3,410) is likely dead; pet (~1,030), biocontrol, pollination/honey, exhibit and aquarium are likely live; food is unclear. The labels are free text and need tidying (`pet` vs `Pet`, combined values).

## Wang et al. 2023 - butterfly species sold online
- *Biol. Conserv.* 283:110092, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biocon.2023.110092 (CC-BY). PDF: `Wang_2023_butterfly_species_sold_online.pdf`.
- Data availability (from PDF): "(1) All annotated butterfly transaction data; (2) species-level trait data used for price and volume predictions and (3) representative image clusters are deposited on Zenodo"
- Zenodo: https://zenodo.org/records/7825674 (README + **3** CSVs: SM1 species traits/volume/price, SM2 51,348 transactions 15.2 MB, SM3 image clusters). MD5 verified.
- GitHub (scraper code): https://github.com/Weilin37/ButterflyTradeEbay
- **Local:** SM2 covers all of 2022, eBay, with seller location. 873 sellers, names replaced by IDs. Top countries: DE, PL, GB, RU, US. **No Norwegian sellers.**
- **Limitation:** the listing titles suggest pinned or framed specimens, i.e. **dead**. Treat as evidence of trade, not of live-pest risk.

## Marshall et al. 2022 - arachnid trade
- *Commun. Biol.* 5:448, doi 10.1038/s42003-022-03374-0. PDF: `Marshall_2022_arachnid_trade.pdf`.
- Data availability (from PDF): "All data are available as supplements to this manuscript. Data used to produce figures and summary data are also available at [Zenodo]. Code used is available at [Zenodo]."
- Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5758540 and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5758541 point to the same 26 files (Data S1–S13, Code S01–S12). All downloaded, MD5 verified.
- Also on PMC: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9120460
- **Main value is the method:** Code S01–S05 (find sale websites with search engines, get the pages, build keywords from species names and synonyms, search the pages for them) is an R pipeline for step 2. Data S1 flags whether each website allows automated searching (useful for the terms-of-service question).

## LEMIS 2000–2014 (Eskew et al. 2020)
- github.com/eveskew/lemis release v1.1.0, `lemis.fst` (205 MB). `kephelps/LEMIS` on rdrr.io is a fork of the same package.
- Live codes: `LIV` live, `EGL` live eggs, `DEA` shipped live but died in transit. Company name fields are not read.
- **US imports only, and only up to 2014.**

- 443,766 live non-vertebrate import records, 189,179 with a species name. **767 species imported live (174 insects)**, 73 of them with an EPPO code.
- Top live insects by shipments: *Papilio dardanus* (1,097), *P. nireus*, *P. demodocus*, *Heliconius hecale*, *H. melpomene*, *H. erato*, *Morpho peleides* (445,365 individuals), mostly from CR, KE, TZ and PH.
- Live and EPPO-listed: *Papilio demoleus* (243 shipments, 4,414 individuals), *Cydia pomonella* (1 shipment), *Dactylopius coccus* (1), *Eriocheir sinensis* (36, EU IAS of Union concern). *Achatina fulica* was imported live but is not in the Hughes list.

## Findings so far
- **Live pet ants are the clearest regulated live insect trade.** *Solenopsis invicta*, *S. geminata*, *Wasmannia auropunctata* and *Pachycondyla chinensis* are sold as colonies. Ant-keeping shops are the priority for step 2. *Pomacea* apple snails (EPPO A1/A2) are also sold live as pets.
- **Several regulated insects (16 species) are traded in unknown form.** Edible insects (*Spodoptera frugiperda*, palm weevils) may be sold live or processed. Most of the others have only the Hughes flags.
- ***Popillia japonica*, *Anoplophora chinensis* and *Cacyreus marshalli* show only dead trade** (specimens, jewellery), so they are labelled dead.
- **Live, plant-relevant, but not regulated in NO/EU:** *Papilio demoleus* (citrus pest, 243 live US shipments), *Cydia pomonella*, giant African snails (*Lissachatina fulica*, *Achatina achatina*, *Archachatina* spp.), *Theba pisana*, *Cornu aspersum*, *Harmonia axyridis*, and many biocontrol agents (EPPO PM 6/3).
- **Most traded insects are dead:** 3,291 of 6,109 insect species have only dead evidence (eBay specimens, collections, LEMIS bodies).
- 3,836 Hughes names flagged `LEMIS` were never imported live. 389 live-imported LEMIS species are not in the Hughes list.
- **Shops:** of 710 found so far, keyword labels give 345 live, 332 unknown, 19 dead and 14 check.
